votes.motion: Ratify the town manager's appointment of Charlotte Chiazzo as seasonal lifeguard and Peter Schmidt as seasonal cemetery laborer.
Adopt the updated environmentally preferable purchasing policy.
Support the letter to the conference committee urging retention of the Foundation Budget Review Commission language in the FY27 budget and additional funding for key areas.

Approve minutes from the January 12, 2026 Tri-Board meeting, January 27, 2026 Tri-Board meeting, March 10, 2026 Tri-Board meeting, May 12, 2026 Select Board meeting, May 12 executive session (not for release), May 20, 2025 Select Board meeting, and June 9, 2025 Select Board meeting.

Enter executive session, not to return to open session, pursuant to Mass. General Laws chapter 30 section 21 A(2), for strategy sessions preparing for negotiations with non-union personnel (facilities director, HR director, director of public works, Lunenburg Council on Aging director, executive assistant to the select board and town manager).

budget_items.topic: Food pantry site septic repair (School Street site)
budget_items.what_was_said: A title five inspection done that day gave the septic system a provisional pass, with a potential repair cost, but was otherwise described as in decent shape.

The finance director asked to postpone fiscal year-end transfers, which move money between departments (e.g., from the health insurance line to a department line running short), until July; such transfers require votes of both the Select Board and Finance Committee by July 15.

budget_items.topic: Flat Hill Road Bridge construction contract
budget_items.what_was_said: The town awarded the construction contract to Kodiak, the second low bidder, after the original awarded contractor could not perform and the apparent low bidder on the rebid was bypassed for a defect.

Lunenburg participates in a state recycling dividends grant program earning points, convertible to grant funds, contingent on annually circulating an environmentally preferable purchasing policy to staff.

budget_items.topic: State minimum school aid per pupil / Foundation Budget Review Commission
budget_items.what_was_said: The letter of support states the House and Senate increased minimum aid per pupil above the Governor's proposed figure, and urges the conference committee to fund the higher of the two proposed levels for special education circuit breaker reimbursement and unrestricted general government aid.
The School Committee's facility staff reported savings achieved through competitive bidding of maintenance contracts, per Brian's committee report.

budget_items.topic: School override defeat and budget concerns
budget_items.what_was_said: The School Committee heard public comment about the recent override defeat, school funding concerns, and athletic and music program concerns, and discussed potential additional state aid and a possible special town meeting ahead of the school year.

budget_items.topic: FY27 tax commitments / neighborhood valuation review
budget_items.what_was_said: The Board of Assessors reported completion of preliminary FY27 tax commitments and described an ongoing neighborhood review project, prompted by Department of Revenue recommendations, focused partly on waterfront property valuations.

transfers.description: Year-end transfers between department lines (e.g., health insurance line to a shortfall department line)
transfers.outcome: discussed only; postponed to July per finance director's request

decisions.decision: Group looking at food pantry temporary sites coalesced around the School Street site as preferable to the TC Passios site, contingent on the school committee agreeing to move T-ball to the TC Passios area.
Town manager and superintendent agreed to a regularly scheduled (about monthly) cadence of finance/leadership meetings between town and school staff.
Board indicated it would proceed with a standalone, formal public hearing on the dangerous/nuisance dog complaint rather than closing the matter on the investigative report alone.
The environmentally preferable purchasing policy will be re-circulated/re-voted only when the policy changes, not annually.
Goals workshop for the Select Board and Town Manager scheduled for July 14th.
Dangerous dog hearing tentatively placeholder-planned for July 28th, pending coordination with the parties involved; may slip to August.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Select Board ratified two seasonal appointments, adopted an updated environmentally preferable purchasing policy, and voted to support a legislative letter urging retention of the Foundation Budget Review Commission and higher school aid levels in the FY27 state budget. The town manager reported progress on a temporary food pantry site at the former School Street school, the awarded Flat Hill Road Bridge contract, and a dangerous/nuisance dog complaint headed to a standalone hearing; the board also scheduled a July 14 goals workshop, approved several sets of prior minutes, heard numerous committee reports, and voted to enter executive session on non-union personnel matters.
